subject: Urgent: policy routing denial wave impacting CarePath production
messages:
From: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@carepath.health>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-09T02:20:00Z
Subject: Production errors: repeated 429s and timeouts (since 02:10 UTC)

Aditya —

We started seeing a sharp spike in 429s and downstream timeouts in our nightly processing at ~02:10 UTC. This is affecting both inference and retry workers; some flows are failing end-to-end. I attached a short log excerpt (errors_20271109.log) and a Grafana snapshot indicating a sudden jump in 429 count and a correlated rise in client-side retries.

Impact: several scheduled jobs failed (billing & claims enrichment pipeline). Latency climbed to >6s per request and our retry logic replayed bursts into your API which looks like a retry storm.

We need an immediate mitigation (temporary throttle relief / emergency quota increase) while you investigate root cause. Please advise next steps and timeline.

-Tim

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@carepath.health>
Date: 2027-11-09T02:31:00Z
Subject: RE: Production errors: repeated 429s and timeouts (since 02:10 UTC)

Thanks for the alert, Tim — and sorry for the hit. Monica & Marissa: can you triage and apply immediate mitigations (temporary quota bump + disable aggressive client retries) while Rishi looks into infra traces?

Initial hypothesis from quick telemetry: large portion of the traffic is being routed to a project alias that was recently re-mapped during a tier migration. The org->project tier mapping appears inconsistent between the billing profile and the runtime throttle policy; that can surface as an unexpected per-project quota cap for some of CarePath's requests which then trigger client retries.

Immediate asks:
- Monica: Apply a short (1h) emergency quota increase for CarePath's org and push a fallback route to the lower-cost model variant so the pipeline doesn't stall.
- Marissa: Draft an external-facing status note we can send to Ops with ETA.
- Rishi: Grab the route logs and ratelimiter counters for the relevant project ids, and confirm whether a mapping table rollback occurred around 01:45–02:00 UTC.

I'll stay on this thread.

—Aditya
Head of Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@carepath.health>
Date: 2027-11-09T02:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Production errors: repeated 429s and timeouts (since 02:10 UTC)

Tim — we've applied the emergency quota bump and disabled client-side aggressive retries on your account (scoped changes) as of 02:40 UTC. You should see reduced 429s within a few minutes; we also routed a fraction of traffic to the fallback model variant to protect throughput.

Attached: quota-mapping-dump.json (redacted) and limit_snapshot.csv — these show that ~40% of CarePath's requests were being matched to an orphaned project alias that carries a conservative org cap. That alias was unintentionally created during last week's tier migration and was not present in the billing service mapping.

Next steps (ops & infra):
- Rishi: confirm whether the mapping table rollback or an incomplete migration caused the alias to be active at runtime.
- Naomi: coordinate a short Post-Mortem with CarePath CS and your engineering contact; include the change window and fix plan.

Let me know if you need further immediate adjustments.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, naomi_feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Jenkins <tim.jenkins@carepath.health>
Date: 2027-11-09T07:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Production errors: repeated 429s and timeouts (since 02:10 UTC) — exec summary and next actions

Quick exec summary for leadership:
- Event: sudden 429 surge and increased latency for CarePath production at ~02:10 UTC, leading to retry amplification and pipeline failures.
- Root cause (prelim): project alias created during a tier migration was not synchronized between billing and runtime routing, resulting in an unexpected per-project cap.
- Impact: transient but customer-visible failures in scheduled processing; CarePath requested immediate relief and was given an emergency quota bump + fallback routing.
- Mitigation: emergency quota increase applied; temporary routing to fallback model; disabled client aggressive retries.
- Remaining actions:
  1) Rishi to patch the reconciliation job to assert strong consistency between billing mapping and runtime routing by EOD and backfill missing aliases. (INF-9247)
  2) Naomi/Monica to run a customer-facing post-mortem and propose a compensation/credit ask; sample DocuSign link attached for expedited approvals.
  3) Product: add a pre-rollout validation checklist for tier migrations to catch alias drift.

Rishi: please confirm ETA for the reconciliation patch and whether we need a hotfix rollback option for future migrations. I will brief leadership if we need to surface this as a wider rollout pause.

—Marissa
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
